intent_and_evidence: Resolvers must not depend on Next.js req/res. createTRPCContext extracts the protocol-specific data once (getServerAuthSession(req,res)) and hands a protocol-independent object {session, prisma} to every middleware and resolver via the ctx argument; createInnerTRPCContext exists so tests can build the same object without HTTP (comment trpc.ts:37-46). Middleware can return a refined context (enforceUserIsAuthed narrows session to non-null). Resolvers get their collaborators (database client, caller identity) only from ctx.

intent_and_evidence: How Date, Map or undefined values cross the HTTP boundary is an interchangeable algorithm. tRPC calls only transformer.serialize/deserialize; with no option it uses the identity defaultTransformer (JSON loses Date), the app selects superjson on both sides so a Date such as user.stripeCurrentPeriodEnd arrives as a Date. Swapping the strategy changes the wire format without touching any procedure. Server and client must choose the same strategy - a configuration constraint the pattern makes explicit.

intent_and_evidence: The search box must react to events that happen anywhere on the page. Instead of the page calling the input, the component subscribes listener objects to document/window; the browser notifies every registered listener on each event and the component unsubscribes on unmount (cleanup functions), so subject and observers stay decoupled and no listener leaks. Distinct from the Zustand observers: the subject is the browser EventTarget and the notification carries a DOM Event.

intent_and_evidence: Async server pages suspend while getShows waits for eight TMDB requests. Because (shows)/loading.tsx exists, Next wraps the segment in <Suspense fallback={<ShowsLoading/>}> so a skeleton is streamed immediately and replaced when the page resolves. The two explicit <Suspense> wrappers in account/users/[userId]/page.tsx and help-center/page.tsx are NOT counted: their children are client components that never suspend, so the fallback can never show (rejected candidate).

intent_and_evidence: A home page needs eight independent lists. getShows broadcasts all requests at once (Promise.all), waits for every reply, applies one all-or-nothing completeness rule (any non-ok response throws) and aggregates the replies into a single result keyed by row; getNewAndPopularShows does the same for four lists. Latency becomes the slowest call instead of the sum. Separate from the TMDB Catalogue Facade, which is about hiding endpoint details; this collaboration is about concurrent fan-out and aggregation.

intent_and_evidence: Profiles and the current user are read by many screens; with staleTime Infinity each key (profile.getAll, profile.getOthers[id], profile.getOne[id], user.getCurrent) is fetched once and then served from the QueryClient. Every mutation that changes those records explicitly invalidates the affected keys (apiUtils.profile.getAll.invalidate() etc.), so the next read goes through to the loader. Independent of the My List Query Cache: different keys, loaders, readers and invalidation points; only the cache store is shared.
